context.situation: You've had toothache for three days. You phone a dental clinic to get an appointment, but you work until five every day.
context.situation_ar: لديك ألم في الأسنان منذ ثلاثة أيام. تتصل بعيادة أسنان لتحصل على موعد، لكنك تعمل حتى الخامسة كل يوم.
context.goal: Make, check and change an appointment on the phone, using polite requests.
context.goal_ar: أن تحجز موعدًا وتؤكده وتغيّره عبر الهاتف باستخدام طلبات مهذبة.

script.t: Good morning, Riverside Dental Clinic. Jenny speaking.
Hi. I'd like to make an appointment, please. I've had toothache since Sunday.
Oh dear. Are you already a patient with us?
OK. Could you give me your full name?
Thanks. We've got something tomorrow at two fifteen. Does that suit you?
I'm afraid I work until five. Would it be possible to come a bit later?
Let me check… Tomorrow evening we're fully booked, but I can offer Thursday at five thirty.
Thursday at half five is perfect. Could you send me a text to confirm?
Of course. And if you need to reschedule, just call us at least a day before.

options: Amir books an appointment for Thursday evening.
Amir can't get an appointment this week.

options: It's too early in the morning.

detail.text: Tomorrow evening the clinic is fully ___.

inference.prompt: Why does the receptionist say "Oh dear"?
options: To show sympathy about his pain

notice.quote: Could you give me your full name? … Would it be possible to come a bit later?

question.prompt: Amir could say "Can I come later?" Why does he say "Would it be possible to come a bit later?"
options: It's more polite — he's asking for a change.

notice.explain: Longer = more polite. Could you…? / Would it be possible to…? / I was wondering if… are useful when you ask a favour or a change.

explain.1: For a length of time we use for: for three days.

notice.explain: since + starting point (since Sunday, since 2020) · for + length of time (for three days).
notice.explain_ar: since مع نقطة البداية، for مع المدة.

grammar.title: Polite requests
grammar.context: Could you give me your full name? — Would it be possible to come a bit later?
grammar.pattern: Could you + verb …? · Would it be possible to + verb …? · Do you think you could + verb …?
examples: Would it be possible to change my appointment?
Do you think you could send me a text?
Could I have something later in the day?
grammar.explain: The bigger the favour, the longer and softer the request.
grammar.explain_ar: كلما كبر الطلب، كانت الصيغة أطول وألطف.

errors.why: For times and arrangements we say suit: Does that suit you?

practice.sentence: I've had toothache since three days.
answers: I've had toothache for three days.
I have had toothache for three days.
practice.why: "Three days" is a length of time, so use for.

pronunciation.title: Word stress

pronunciation.title: Polite or rude?
pronunciation.tip: A request that falls flat can sound rude. A wider, rising tone sounds friendlier.
